# The null reference U_null: window in counts, predictive threshold, gradients, recounts

Generated by `scripts/s8_unull.py` (run time 63 s). Evidence class: **calculated** (exact lattice convolution of the decision statistic, summed over the Poisson distribution of the window count) and, for the ros2_ws probe, **simulated** (`scripts/probe_unull_windows.py` on the simulator scenarios; not re-run by `run_all.sh`). All coefficients are synthetic demonstration values; nothing is measured. Verdicts and proposed MODEL.md wording: `../MODEL_REVIEW_rev4.md`.

Statistic: one lane of the revision-4 linear statistic, beta window (k = 1, b = 0.5 s⁻¹, u(k) 0.003 lane ⊕ 0.03 common, u(b) = 0.054 s⁻¹), scan cell 1 s (weights 1; a realistic centred footprint gives the same ratios within 0.02, lower) and stationary recounts of 10, 30 and 60 s. Dose rates as parameterised in the package (33.2 s⁻¹ per µSv/h). Recount α of the demonstration two-stage profile: 1.71e-4; mission-level α 1.14e-5.

"Live" is the last evaluation the processor made while the mission ran (the exported value); "final" is one evaluation of every cell at the end with all reference data. Mechanisms, from `rr_core/processing.py` `_u_null`:

1. **Evaluation schedule (implementation).** A cell is re-evaluated only when it gains gates, with the reference data received so far, so the window is truncated at "now" and frozen into the export (independent review C1).
2. **Symmetric window around each gate, per attachment series (implementation).** The window is ±100·T_F around every gate under test, within one attachment's reference series. A head reset starts a new series, and a cell near a series start or end cannot reach 200·T_F even when the other side holds minutes of data.
3. **Requirement in seconds proportional to T_F (rule).** Multi-pass and slow-scan cells have T_F of 1–6 s and need 200–1200 s of reference, whatever the count rate. The same rule accepts edge cells with small T_F on fewer than 50 counts, which is too few for the plug-in threshold at small α.

## 2. What the threshold needs from U_null: counts

The null mean of the statistic is zero for any U (the same-gate reference is subtracted); U_null fixes only the shape of the null distribution. A window of N counts gives U_null a relative error of 1/√N, so the plug-in threshold moves by z·g·δ/2 null standard deviations, where g = d ln Var₀/d ln U (1 for counting-dominated statistics, up to 2 when U²u²(k) dominates). To second order the inflation is exp(z⁴g²/(8N)), so the requirement depends on N, α and g, not on T_F. The exact results:

- **Plug-in** (revision 4): N_ref for ≤ 1.05 at mission α up to 1.00e+03 for scan cells and 2.70e+03 for recounts (≤ 1.10: 512 for scans); the formula predicts the exact values to within about 20 %.
- **Predictive threshold** (null distribution averaged over the Jeffreys posterior Gamma(N + ½, T_w) of U; in Gil-Pelaez form, the average of the characteristic functions over 12 posterior nodes): N_ref for ≤ 1.05 at mission α ≤ 98.8 for scans, ≤ 175 for recounts (largest case: 60 s at 3 µSv/h, where U²u²(k) dominates and g = 1.7); at α = 0.05, 25 counts (the lower end of the grid) suffice. Over the whole grid, at most 175 counts for ≤ 1.05.
- **One-sided against centred:** the precision is that of the count; the side does not matter. The two differ only under field variation (section 4).
- **Independence** matters because of correlation, not precision: the same-gate pool fails at any length (revision-3 checks, 21.5× per lane).

### 2.1 Pooled four-lane window: lane response ratio

A pooled window estimates the mean of the four lanes' reference rates. A lane whose reference reads 1 % above the pool is assigned a U_null 1 % low:

| µSv/h | α | N_ref (pooled) | lane response 5 % below pool | 2 % below | 1 % below | equal | 2 % above | 5 % above |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.100 | 0.05 | 200 | 1.07 | 1.03 | 1.01 | 0.999 | 0.969 | 0.926 |
| 0.100 | 0.05 | 3.20e+03 | 1.07 | 1.03 | 1.01 | 1.000 | 0.971 | 0.928 |
| 0.100 | 1.14e-05 | 200 | 1.41 | 1.16 | 1.08 | 1.01 | 0.885 | 0.725 |
| 0.100 | 1.14e-05 | 3.20e+03 | 1.41 | 1.14 | 1.07 | 1.00 | 0.877 | 0.717 |
| 1.00 | 0.05 | 200 | 1.09 | 1.04 | 1.02 | 1.00 | 0.971 | 0.923 |
| 1.00 | 0.05 | 3.20e+03 | 1.09 | 1.03 | 1.02 | 1.00 | 0.967 | 0.919 |
| 1.00 | 1.14e-05 | 200 | 1.60 | 1.22 | 1.12 | 1.02 | 0.854 | 0.654 |
| 1.00 | 1.14e-05 | 3.20e+03 | 1.58 | 1.20 | 1.10 | 1.00 | 0.835 | 0.635 |

At mission α: 1 % ratio error 1.12, 2 % 1.22, 5 % 1.60. A pooled window must therefore be scaled by each lane's reference-rate ratio, estimated over the attachment record, and the ratio's statistical uncertainty enters the posterior (effective count 1/(1/N_pool + 1/n_lane,run + 1/n_all,run)). A ratio that differs locally (a lateral field gradient across the 0.26 m head) is a bias this cannot remove; that is the reason to prefer the lane's own window.

The predictive threshold costs at most 1.07 in D# at 50 counts, 1.04 at 100 and 1.01 at 400. The provably conservative rule (U at the upper 1 − α/10 Poisson bound, threshold at 0.9α) costs up to 1.32 at 100 counts and holds α with a large margin (achieved/nominal 0.03–0.4); it is not recommended.

Including the window count as a term of the statistic (replacing or supplementing the same-gate reference with N_window) also gives a null mean independent of U, and a lower variance. But it compares the floor with a reference taken elsewhere or at another time, which is the uncompensated estimator's weakness. The statistic keeps the same-gate reference, and the window enters only through the threshold.

## 3. Field gradients (scan at 0.1 m/s)

Window of 175 counts (the largest predictive requirement at mission α, all statistics). Length of travel: lane window 5.27 m at 0.1 µSv/h and 0.527 m at 1 µSv/h; pooled 1.32 m and 0.132 m. The field rises along travel (worst sign for a past-only window); steps sit at the cell edge in the worst orientation. Worst achieved/nominal at mission α: centred mean 12.2 (steps; 12.2), past-only mean 120, larger of the two half-window means 1.03 (cost in D# at most 1.05 × the unbiased value). A centred mean is exact for a linear gradient but not for a step. The larger of the past and future half-window means is never biased low by a step or a monotone gradient, and costs little.

During a recount the other three lanes' references count the same field, at the same place and time, and are not part of the m = 1 statistic. With ratio scaling they provide 100–18 000 counts in 10–60 s, more than the predictive threshold needs in every case, so no bracketing time is needed (extra time 0 s). If only the lane's own reference is accepted, the bracketing time is 0.704–23.7 s per recount (about 14–24 s at 0.1 µSv/h, ≤ 4 s at ≥ 1 µSv/h).
